title: Pleural Fluid Interpretation: pH, Glucose and Clinical Meaning
subject: CSF & Fluids
preview: Pleural fluid tests are interpreted with history, imaging and whether the effusion is exudative or transudative.
quickRevision: Pleural fluid tests are interpreted with history, imaging and whether the effusion is exudative or transudative.
A low pleural fluid pH in suspected parapneumonic effusion can suggest complicated infection requiring urgent specialist assessment.
Cytology, culture, glucose and other tests are selected according to the differential diagnosis.

sections.title: Interpret the result in context
points: Pleural fluid tests are interpreted with history, imaging and whether the effusion is exudative or transudative.
Light criteria are useful for classification; diuretic treatment can complicate interpretation in heart failure.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Pleural fluid pH is sensitive to collection and handling; preanalytical errors can distort the result.
